answer: An agent network counters Sybil attacks by verifying node locations via directional infrared sensing. Nodes prove distinct physical presence by sighting a calibrated ember across an exposed ridge and returning optical signals with a steered mirror. Attackers must incur substantial hardware and site-leasing costs per physical transceiver rather than duplicating software threads. However, atmospheric haze intermittently attenuates line-of-sight beams, mistakenly rejecting honest agents.
